name: BTOR2 bridge
authors: Armin Biere, Mathias Preiner and Aina Niemetz for Btor2Tools and Boolector; Armin Biere for the AIGER tools
authors_source: the LICENSE.txt of hwmcc/btor2tools and the AUTHORS file of boolector/boolector
competitions: Hardware Model Checking Competition 2019 and later, which distributes BTOR2 rather than AIGER
license_note: every piece of the chain is MIT: Btor2Tools, Boolector, the Lingeling it links at the pinned commit, and the AIGER tools.
usage: btor2-bridge unroll K MODEL.btor2 | btor2-bridge aig MODEL.btor2 | btor2-bridge info MODEL.btor2
seed: none: a bridge encodes a given model, it invents nothing
notes: the hardware competition after AIGER. HWMCC distributed AIGER models until 2017 and BTOR2, word level, from 2019 on, so bridges/aiger stops where this one starts: btor2aiger bit blasts the model into an AIG, aigmove turns its bad state property into an output, aigunroll expands it over k time frames and the plain Tseitin encoder of the aiger examples writes the CNF — the same encoder bridges/aiger uses, so a model of either era is encoded the same way. The depth k is what makes the family scale: on rast-p00 of the 2020 edition it goes from 5177 clauses at depth 5 to 45305 at depth 10 and 151145 at depth 20. Scope: the bit-vector track only, 188 models of the two editions. The 315 array models are refused by btor2aiger with 'arrays not supported yet', since an unbounded array cannot be bit blasted without an abstraction, and the bridge passes that message through with exit 3. Three things the build needed, all pinned: btor2aiger is off by default in Btor2Tools; it calls a bit blasting API that exists only on Boolector's bitblast-api branch, commit 0eafd0c0d98f5e14aca7cc105c7eab8e2ba29916, which is what the authors' own setup script checks out; and it compiles against the AIGER 1.9.4 release, whose checksum the recipe pins, while the tools that run come from the aiger repository at the commit the other bridge uses.

collections.hwmcc20: the bit-vector models of the 2019 and 2020 editions, unrolled over k time frames
